problem: Reduce poverty and its health effects.
title: Brazil launches Bolsa Familia, a conditional cash transfer for poor households
context: Brazil had widespread poverty and child mortality related to poverty.
decision_made: Pay cash to poor households on condition that they meet health and education requirements.
action_taken: Launched in 2003 as a nationwide programme.
observed_outcome: A 2025 Lancet Public Health study found the programme prevented over 8.2 million hospitalisations and 713,083 deaths between 2004 and 2019, though effects faded when transfers stopped. A 2013 Lancet analysis found it contributed to lower childhood mortality. One study found only weak links with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality.
lessons: Conditional cash transfers can improve health outcomes at national scale, with effects that depend on continued payment.
limitations: These are observational studies that attribute effects with statistical models. Results on school attendance and poverty were not covered in the sources used. A separate study found weak mortality associations.

claims.claim_text: Brazil's Bolsa Familia is a conditional cash transfer programme launched in 2003.
A Lancet Public Health study estimated the programme prevented 8.2 million hospitalisations and 713,083 deaths between 2004 and 2019.
